newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX edges up on gains to several blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX edges up on gains to several blue chips.

text.p: Gains to several blue chips pulled the SAX index up 0.26 points to 195.03 in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday.
Steel maker VSZ was the most heavily traded share, with 5,787 shares changing hands, but it closed unchanged at 750 crowns.

"The (VSZ) price will remain steady until the AGM on May 21, and today's volume was mainly an arbitrage on different prices on the BSE and the over-the-counter market," said Bohus Betko of ING Barings.
Oil and gas storage firm Nafta and the largest commercial bank VUB both rose five crows to close at 1,455 and 1,505 crowns respectively.
Betko said trading was generally very thin, but added that greater volumes were to be expected after the end of the AGM season next month.
"There are virtualy only two issue with higher liquidity on the BSE at present - VSZ and Slovnaft - but we expect more active trading to resume after shareholders meetings," he said.
Overall, volume fell to 92,416 shares, from 163,108 stocks traded on Monday, while turnover rose to 54.63 million crowns from 43.44 million.
